title: A Man Who Walked with God

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: This is the account of Noah and his family. Noah was a righteous man, blameless among the people of his time, and he walked faithfully with God. - Gen 6:9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Having found grace, Noah now lives a life shaped by it. He is described in three ways: righteous, blameless, and one who "walked faithfully with God" - the same phrase used of Enoch. This was a life of consistent, God-centred integrity in the middle of a deeply corrupt generation.

We should not misunderstand "blameless." It does not mean Noah was sinless or perfect; later chapters show his failures. It means his life was one of integrity and genuine faith - he belonged to God and walked with Him honestly. His righteousness flowed from the grace he had received, not the other way around.

What makes Noah's example so striking is his setting. He was righteous "among the people of his time" - a time when "every inclination" of hearts was evil. He did not drift with the current of his culture. Surrounded by wickedness, he walked with God anyway.

That is a challenge for every believer. It is possible to walk faithfully with God even when everyone around us has abandoned Him. We are called to be "blameless and pure, children of God without fault in a warped and crooked generation" in which we "shine... like stars" (Phil 2:15). We cannot do this in our own strength, but by the same grace that found Noah, God enables us to walk with Him in any generation, however dark.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you walking with God, or drifting with your culture?
- What would it take to keep your integrity in an ungodly environment?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, like Noah, help me walk faithfully with You even when the world around me does not. By Your grace, keep me blameless and shining for You in this generation.
